question: In England and Wales, what is the legal breath-alcohol limit for drivers?
options: 22 microgrammes per 100 ml of breath
50 microgrammes per 100 ml of breath
80 microgrammes per 100 ml of breath
35 microgrammes per 100 ml of breath
explanation: Do not drink and drive as it will seriously affect your judgement and abilities. In England and Wales you MUST NOT drive with a breath alcohol level higher than 35 microgrammes/100 millilitres of breath or a blood alcohol level of more than 80 milligrammes/100 millilitres of blood. (Highway Code rule 95.)

question: When should you give a signal to other road users?
options: Immediately before you start the manoeuvre
Only when other vehicles are close behind
Only when turning right
In plenty of time, after checking it would not be misleading
explanation: Signals warn and inform other road users of your intended actions. Give clear signals in plenty of time, having checked it is not misleading to signal at that time. (Highway Code rule 103.)

question: According to the Highway Code, when should you flash your headlights?
options: Only to let other road users know you are there
To thank another driver
To warn of a speed camera ahead
To tell another driver to go ahead
explanation: Flashing headlights. Only flash your headlights to let other road users know that you are there. Do not flash your headlights to convey any other message or intimidate other road users. (Highway Code rule 110.)

question: Between which hours MUST you NOT sound your horn in a built-up area, except to avoid danger?
options: 11.00 pm and 8.00 am
10.00 pm and 6.00 am
11.30 pm and 7.00 am
Midnight and 6.30 am
explanation: The horn. Use only while your vehicle is moving and you need to warn other road users of your presence. Never sound your horn aggressively. You MUST NOT use your horn while stationary on the road, or when driving in a built-up area between the hours of 11.30 pm and 7.00 am, except when another road user poses a danger. (Highway Code rule 112.)

options: Only when another road user poses a danger

explanation: The horn. Use only while your vehicle is moving and you need to warn other road users of your presence. Never sound your horn aggressively. You MUST NOT use your horn while stationary on the road, or when driving in a built-up area between the hours of 11.30 pm and 7.00 am, except when another road user poses a danger. question: You are waiting in your car for a passenger. What does the Highway Code say about leaving the engine running?
options: It is fine for up to five minutes
It is fine if you stay in the vehicle
It is only an offence in a smoke-control area
You MUST NOT leave the engine running unnecessarily while stationary on a public road
explanation: The driver and the environment. You MUST NOT leave a parked vehicle unattended with the engine running or leave a vehicle engine running unnecessarily while that vehicle is stationary on a public road. (Highway Code rule 123.)

question: Which of these is a specific offence under the Road Traffic Act referred to in the Highway Code?
options: Driving more slowly than the speed limit
Driving with an untidy interior
Driving with the radio on
Driving without reasonable consideration for other road users
explanation: You MUST NOT drive dangerously, drive without due care and attention, or drive without reasonable consideration for other road users. (Highway Code rule 144.)

question: In slow-moving traffic, what should you do?
options: Use the hard shoulder to make progress
Leave enough room to manoeuvre if the vehicle in front breaks down
Move into the lane that is moving fastest
Drive close to the vehicle in front to stop others cutting in
explanation: In slow-moving traffic you should reduce the distance between you and the vehicle ahead to maintain traffic flow, never get so close that you cannot stop safely, leave enough space to manoeuvre if the vehicle in front breaks down, and not change lanes to the left to overtake. (Highway Code rule 151.)

question: A vehicle behind is trying to overtake you. What should you do?
options: Speed up so they cannot pass
Maintain a steady course and speed, slowing if necessary to let them pass
Move to the centre of the road
Brake sharply to warn them
explanation: Being overtaken. If a driver is trying to overtake you, maintain a steady course and speed, slowing down if necessary to let the vehicle pass. Never obstruct drivers who wish to pass. (Highway Code rule 168.)

question: An emergency vehicle with flashing blue lights is approaching from behind. What should you do?
options: Speed up to clear the road ahead
Consider its likely route and let it pass while still complying with traffic signs
Mount the kerb to get out of the way
Stop immediately wherever you are
explanation: Emergency and Incident Support vehicles. You should look and listen for ambulances, fire engines, police, doctors or other emergency vehicles using flashing blue, red or green lights and sirens. When one approaches, do not panic; consider the route of such a vehicle and take appropriate action to let it pass while complying with all traffic signs. (Highway Code rule 219.)

question: A bus is signalling to pull out from a bus stop ahead of you. What should you do?
options: Pull out and overtake immediately
Sound your horn so it waits
Speed up to pass before it moves
Give way to it if you can do so safely
explanation: Buses, coaches and trams. Give priority to these vehicles when you can do so safely, especially when they signal to pull away from stops. Look out for people getting off a bus or tram and crossing the road. (Highway Code rule 223.)
